better_overall.reason: B is the more polished and welcoming page, gives visitors what they need (where, drop-ins, access, contact) and has the smoother phone booking: a choice of the next three Saturdays, one-tap chips, an email app that opens with the booking filled in, a copy-and-phone fallback and 'Book another item'. Its weak points are an obvious placeholder address, phone and email plus a few invented house rules, all quick for the organiser to replace or check, while A's honest, distinctive page stays austere, has no location or contact details, and adds a second step ('Get your ticket', then 'Email your ticket') where some visitors may stop before actually booking.

post_code_notes: Stage-1 views mostly stand; the code sharpens them. (1) B's 'Note for the organisers' only appears while the booking address is still example.org and no form service is set, so it is a deliberate setup safeguard that also warns visitors before they waste effort, not a permanent blemish. It is still visible as shipped, so the 'looks generated' point stays. (2) A's ticket idea goes further than the screenshots showed: submitting produces a large stubbed 'Your ticket' that states plainly 'This is not a booking yet', and A tells the visitor its address is only an example, after submit. That confirms A as the more distinctive and transparent build. (3) B invents more than the screenshots showed: 'Later slots are usually quieter', last arrivals 12:30, one item per booking, slot holders seen first, no volunteers for phones or laptops, a placeholder street and postcode with a live Google Maps link, and a reserved fictional number (01632 960123) offered as 'ring or text us'. This is why B scores 3 for honesty. (4) Both work out the first Saturday, move to the next one after 1pm and support skip dates. A's no-JavaScript fallback is a hard-coded 'Saturday 3 October' that will go stale; B falls back to 'First Saturday of every month'. (5) Neither can cap how many people book each slot: both send an email request that a volunteer confirms. B adds a hook for a form-service endpoint and a spam trap. A has the stronger error handling (an error summary at the top that takes focus, plus inline messages); B has inline errors that move focus to the first problem. Contrast passes AA throughout both sites. (Aside: comments were not fully stripped from either site's JS; they do not reveal who built it.)
